$Comment: What the Horseman's Hoard (Rewards/Hallows_Eve/Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Chase) pays for the first win
on the normal ride each day. Every roll is read on its own: the first has no Chance, so it always
pays and the Hoard is never empty; the next is the chance at a Grave Candle, which gives back what
opening the graveyard costs; the four after it are the chances at the Flaming Hallowed set's
pieces (the Burning Jack Helm, the Horseman's flaming gauntlets and greaves, and the Flaming Jack
Shield); then two pieces of his graveyard to build with, a tombstone and a ruins lantern like the
ones that stand in it, which no recipe makes and which pay from this Hoard alone; the last always
pays Old Jack's Favor, so the normal ride is a way toward the Regular rank that opens the hard
ride. The hard ride's Hoard (Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Chase_Hard.json) pays more Grave Candles, the
Flaming pieces at better odds, his flaming breastplate and the Eternal Candle, and the Hallowed's
favor instead of Old Jack's; Mmo_Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Chase.json adds Defense XP where MMO Skill
Tree runs. His plain armour pays from his daily Claim (Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Daily.json). The
Almanac's Hoard grid (ZiggfreedCommon/Almanac/HallowsEvePack/Hallows_Eve.json) lists what this
table and the hard one pay, so change them together. Chance is a percent from 0 to 100.
HideInPreview on the four Flaming pieces keeps them out of any list of what this table pays (a
reward paying it lists its contents on hover); the Hoard itself lands as a Claim of what it
rolled, and the rolls pay the same either way.
Name: Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Chase
